body:
Greetings all,

If you would like to subscribe to a secure, anonymous, email mailing-
list which I, *and only I*, will be able to use to notify people of
news updates on the UNABOM case and trial, please send email to:

ehaugsja@cs.umass.edu 

with:

subscribe unanews your_email@address.here FirstName LastName

(for example: subscribe unanews ehaugsja@cs.umass.edu Erika Haugsja)

in the body of the message.  

And feel free to share any thoughts on any aspect of the case below this
"subscribe" line.  I'd be interested to hear...

(Of course... you can be certain that I will give your address to no
one.  Except for the FBI or JCrew.  I can't really say no to either of
them if they ask.  They're both always *so nice* on the phone! :)

E

SacBee, Wed, July 30, 1997, Cynthia Hubert 
(originally broke on 29th by Rich Harris, AP, but better explained here)
   Theodore Kaczynski's personal journals cannot be excluded from his
   Sacramento trial based on arguments that his private thoughts are
   protected under the U.S. Constitution, a federal judge has ruled.

   But U.S. District Judge Garland E. Burrell Jr. said he will consider 
   a late challenge to the FBI's search of the suspected Unabomber's
   mountain cabin, which yielded the diaries and other evidence.

AP, Thu, July 31, 1997, Rich Harris
   ... The government on Wednesday asked a judge
   to order Unabomber suspect Theodore Kaczynski's lawyers to be more
   specific about any insanity defense they might be contemplating.
   ...
   The prosecution also argued that because Kaczynski is putting his
   mental state in question, the government should be allowed to do its
   own examination. Courts have ruled previously that it is unfair to
   allow the defense to offer testimony about a possible mental disease
   or defect without allowing the government an opportunity to rebut the
   evidence.
